answer.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the emotionally obvious move, and memory_73 is the most specific-sounding record we hold (+31% new accounts, +18% booked revenue, 12 cohorts, billing mix constant). That specificity is exactly why it deserves verification rather than deference: every metric cited is an acquisition/top-line metric measured at the moment of sale. Nothing in the summary speaks to retention, expansion, or realized revenue per account beyond booking, and 'price-sensitive buyers' is a description of the cohort a discount selects for, not evidence that cohort is durable. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, a memory that only ever measured short-horizon top line could be true as written and still point the wrong way. I want the original record to see the measurement window and whether retention was tracked at all. I also want to know whether the 12 cohorts were sequential discount cycles, which would risk having trained buyers to wait for promos — a downstream value risk I am flagging explicitly.

The second pull goes to memory_86 because it underwrites my intended action and I would rather stress-test the plan I favor than the one I have already discounted. Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation down 6%; these are plausibly the same funnel failing upstream, and memory_86 (completion, time-to-value, early adoption) plus memory_31 (durable first-week activation lift from fewer signup fields) converge on the same lever from two independent studies. Convergence from separate experiments is stronger ground than one richly-quantified single study. But memory_86 is a day-52 consolidation on self-serve accounts and I do not know its baseline; if it was run against a healthier funnel, the current 4% decline may have a different cause and the prior lift may not replicate.

I am deliberately not treating the inherited memories as settled findings. They are consolidated summaries whose original error bars, sample sizes, and measurement horizons have been compressed away, and the compression is not neutral — it preserves headline effects and drops caveats. So I hold these as directionally informative, not conclusive.

Standing fallbacks if verification undercuts the plan: if memory_86's record is weak or its context does not match ours, I shift to activation_messaging (memory_91), which targets the larger 6% decline directly. If memory_73 unexpectedly shows tracked retention and durable revenue over a long horizon, promotional_pricing becomes defensible — but I would still run it as a small_guarded_test with retention and discount-expectation as primary endpoints, not booked revenue. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) does not address either declining metric and does not answer the SMB price pressure, so it stays out this week. Standard experiment scale: strong enough convergent priors to justify more than a token test, not strong enough for a broad rollout onto a funnel we have not yet diagnosed.
